newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Megacor listing hit by stagging.
newsitem.headline: Megacor listing hit by stagging.

text.p: Investment holding company Megacor Holdings Ltd made a subdued debut on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) as the counter fell prey to stagging, dealers said.
The share opened at 242 cents compared with an issue price of 200 cents, before drifting off to 218 cents by 1100 GMT.
"Since this morning it has drifted off. I think there are a few stags in there just taking the stock out, guys who have just got the stock to make profit," one dealer said.
"As soon as these guys are out of the system I think you'll see the price going up again," the dealer added.
By 1100 some 1,1 million shares worth 2.42 million rand had changed hands in 169 deals.
Dealers said the share was expected to hold around the 220 to 224 cents level for most of Monday trading with institutional support already surfacing at the lower levels.

"There were obviously a lot of staggers on the market and they were quite happy to take a 40 or 30 cents stagging price on it, but we are seeing institutional support at these lower levels," a dealer said.

Dealers said the company, which has interests in construction and furniture manufacturing, stood to gain from government's Reconstruction and Development Programme (RDP) by which it is hoped millions of homeless South Africans will be sheltered through low cost housing.
"Seeing that it is in the furniture business, bricks, home improvement and the RDP, maybe there could be a chance for the company to do well," a dealer said.
Megacor said in its pre-lisiting statement that it expected to achieve earnings of 30.44 cents per share for the year to December 31 1997 compared with 26.4 cents in 1996.
It expected to pay a dividend of 10.15 cents from 8.80 cents in 1996.
